title: Detainees hunger strike over Folkston detention center conditions

tea.why: Detainees are protesting against conditions at the Folkston ICE processing center and violations of asylum processing laws.
tea.want: Better detention conditions and respect for asylum seekers' rights.
tea.changed: Oct 27: Reports noted that a detained Salvadoran man died at the facility, while the hunger strike continued with at least 12 participants remaining on strike.

summary: Detainees at the D. Ray James ICE processing facility in Folkston, Georgia, launched a hunger strike protesting facility conditions and asylum processing practices. According to reports cited by advocacy groups and media, approximately 500 individuals joined the strike at the beginning of October. U.S. Senators Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff subsequently requested an immediate federal investigation into the facility, noting reports of medical neglect and retaliation against strikers, including placement in solitary confinement. Asian Americans Advancing Justice stated that participants faced retaliation and threats of forced feeding. Concurrently, Immigration and Customs Enforcement confirmed the death of a 48-year-old detainee at the complex.
demands: Oppose violations of asylum processing laws
response: U.S. Senators Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff called on the Department of Homeland Security to conduct an immediate inspection and investigation into the facility. ICE issued statements regarding a detainee death and facility operations.

crowd.text: about 500 detainees had gone on a hunger strike

deaths.text: a 48-year-old man from El Salvador, Luis Sandoval, died

updates.text: ICE confirmed the death of a 48-year-old detainee inside the Folkston facility.
U.S. Senators Warnock and Ossoff requested an immediate federal investigation into alleged retaliation and conditions.
Asian Americans Advancing Justice reported that at least 12 people were still refusing food.
